title: CRISPR is now being used to control genes, not just edit them | New Scientist
description: CRISPR-based treatments that work by turning genes on or off are being tested in trials, and could be even more powerful than conventional gene editing
author: Michael Le Page

title: Vagus nerve stimulation slows growth and spread of pancreatic cancer | New Scientist
description: An electrical implant around the oesophagus that stimulates the vagus nerve improved outcomes in mice with pancreatic cancer by making their tumours more susceptible to immunotherapy
author: Carissa Wong

title: Particles not seen before have been observed in a quantum simulator | New Scientist
description: Physicists long held that all particles fall under categories of bosons or fermions, but a new experiment offers evidence that a third and long-debated class is possible after all
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Ultracold atoms could help unravel a major flaw in quantum theory | New Scientist
description: Standard quantum theory struggles to predict how long a particle will take to get from one place to another, but an experiment with ultracold atoms could help rule out some interpretations
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren't broadcasting their location | New Scientist
description: Researchers have found that seabirds equipped with audio recorders and GPS trackers can detect ships, offering a way to monitor fishing vessels that are operating illegally
author: Shosha Adie

title: AI's stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it | New Scientist
description: The biggest problem in maths has been cracked by AI, but it remains impossible to predict how its capabilities will advance in other fields
author: New Scientist
